note.explanation: Allotropy is when an element exists in different structural forms. The forms can have different properties. Carbon has diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene as its main allotropic forms; sulphur has rhombic and monoclinic forms.
examples: Carbon: diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene
note.simple: One element can have different forms because its atoms are arranged differently. These forms may behave differently.

note.answer: Allotropic forms are different structural forms of the same element.

written.text: What are allotropic forms? Explain the allotropic forms of carbon and sulphur. How does coal differ from diamond?
written.finalAnswer: Allotropic forms are different structural forms of the same element. Carbon has diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene (C₆₀) as its main allotropic forms. Diamond has a giant macromolecular structure; graphite has layers of hexagonal rings of carbon; C₆₀ consists of a cage-like sphere of atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons. Sulphur has two crystalline allotropic forms, rhombic and monoclinic; rhombic sulphur is more stable. Coal is an impure, non-crystalline form of carbon, whereas diamond is a crystalline form of carbon with a giant macromolecular structure.

modelAnswer: Allotropic forms are different structural forms of the same element.
Carbon has three main allotropic forms: diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene (C₆₀).
Diamond has a giant macromolecular structure.
Graphite has a layered structure of hexagonal rings of carbon.
Buckminster fullerene (C₆₀) consists of a cage-like sphere of atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons.
Sulphur exists in two crystalline allotropic forms: rhombic and monoclinic sulphur.
Rhombic sulphur is more stable than monoclinic sulphur.
Coal is an impure, non-crystalline form of carbon, whereas diamond is a crystalline form of carbon with a giant macromolecular structure.

explain.title: What allotropy means
explain.body: Elements may exist in more than one structural forms which can exhibit quite different physical and chemical properties. These forms are called allotropic forms and phenomenon is called allotropy.

explain.title: Allotropic forms of oxygen
explain.body: Element oxygen exists in two allotropic forms namely oxygen (O₂) and ozone (O₃).

explain.title: Carbon forms have different structures
explain.body: Carbon exists in three main allotropic forms: diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene. Diamond has a giant macromolecular structure. Graphite has a layered structure of hexagonal rings of carbon. Buckminster fullerene (C₆₀) consists of spheres made of atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons.

explain.title: Sulphur has two crystalline forms
explain.body: Element sulphur also exists in two crystalline allotropic forms i.e. rhombic and monocline; the former is more stable than the latter.

mistakes: Do not confuse an element's allotropic forms with compounds made from that element; for example, O₂ and O₃ are forms of oxygen.
Do not swap the structures: diamond is giant macromolecular, while graphite is layered.
Do not say monoclinic sulphur is more stable; the section says rhombic sulphur is more stable.
When describing fullerene, include its cage-like spherical structure and the pentagons and hexagons.
